message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Step | What Happens | Key Points | |------|--------------|------------| | **1. Setup** | • Shuffle the Uno deck (108 cards).
• Deal 7 cards to each player.
• Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile.
• Flip the top card of the draw pile to start the discard pile. | • If the first card is an action card, its effect applies to the first player. | | **2. Turn Order** | • Players take turns clockwise (or counterclockwise if a “Reverse” card is played). | • The direction changes when a Reverse card is played. | | **3. Playing a Card** | • On your turn, you may play one card from your hand that matches the **color**, **number**, or **symbol** of the top discard.
• If you have no playable card, you must draw one from the draw pile.
• If the drawn card is playable, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | • You can only play one card per turn unless you use a special card that allows multiple plays (e.g., “Draw Two” or “Wild Draw Four”). | | **4. Action Cards** | • **Skip** – Next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – Changes play direction.
• **Draw Two** – Next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
• **Wild** – Player chooses the next color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – Player chooses the next color; next player draws four cards and loses their turn (can be challenged if the player could have played a different card). | • “Wild Draw Four” can only be played if you have no other playable card of the current color. | | **5. Winning a Round** | • The first player to discard all their cards wins the round.
• The winner scores points based on the cards left in opponents’ hands:
 – Number cards: face value
 – Skip/Reverse/Draw Two: 20 points
 – Wild/Wild Draw Four: 50 points | • A round ends when a player reaches 100 points (or another agreed threshold). | | **6. Optional Variations** | • **Stacking** – Some groups allow stacking “Draw Two” or “Wild Draw Four” cards to avoid drawing.
• **Custom Rules** – e.g., “No Draw” where players must play a card or pass. | • Clarify rules before starting. | **Quick Tips** - Keep track of the current color and number to decide what to play. - Use Wild cards strategically to change the color when you’re stuck. - Remember that “Reverse” acts like a “Skip” in a two‑player game. Enjoy playing Uno!
